title: Palworld Best Combat Pals by Element | Fire, Ice, Dragon, Dark and More | Palworld Guide
description: A Palworld 1.0 guide to the strongest fighting Pal for each element, from Jormuntide Ignis and Orserk to Frostallion, Anubis, Necromus, Jetragon and Paladius.

sections.heading: Fighters, not workers
sections.script: Most Palworld guides talk about base workers, but today we look at pure fighters. Which Pal should you bring into a tough battle for each element? This video is based on several current one point zero guides, and I only name picks that more than one source supports. Where the guides disagree, I will tell you, so you can choose for yourself. Remember that the best Pal is not always the one with the biggest attack. It also matters how easy it is to get, how well it uses its partner skill, and whether it fits the boss you face. Let's go element by element and build your dream team of fighters. A quick note on rankings: tier lists change with every patch and every writer has a favorite, so use these picks as a strong starting point and then test them yourself on the bosses you struggle with. A Pal you know well and have leveled will often beat a famous one that sits in your box.

sections.heading: Fire: Jormuntide Ignis
sections.script: For Fire, Jormuntide Ignis shows up in all the guides I checked. It is a Dragon and Fire Pal, and you can ride it. One guide praises its very high melee attack and says its partner skill boosts your Fire attacks. Another ranks it in the top tier for boss fights because of its attack and its strong element mix. It is also one of the easier top fighters to get, since guides note it can be bred rather than hunted as a legendary. One guide picks Blazamut Ryu as the best endgame Fire Pal, so that is a strong alternative if you can get it from a raid. Either way, Fire is a great element to have in your team because many late bosses, such as the Ice boss Bastigor, are weak to it. A Fire fighter you can ride and attack with at the same time is a very comfortable way to play.

sections.heading: Water and Grass
sections.script: Water and Grass are the two elements where the guides disagree most. For Water, one guide picks Jormuntide, the sea mount with a pure Water type, while another prefers Neptilius, which fires water spears when you deal damage. Both are good, so pick whichever you can get first. For Grass, one guide names Lyleen, and another names Verdash, which boosts your speed and gives your attacks a Grass touch. I do not want to pretend there is one answer here. The honest truth is that these two elements are strong as support options and for tower fights, but they are less dominant than the others in the endgame. If you already have one of them leveled up with good passive skills, do not rush to replace it. Passive skills and levels often matter more than the name on the Pal.

sections.heading: Electric: Orserk
sections.script: Electric is an easy call. Two guides name Orserk, a Dragon and Electric Pal with the strongest Electric attack. It is a glass cannon, which means it deals huge damage but it is not the tankiest Pal on your team. Orserk is also one of the few Pals with the top level of the Generating Electricity skill, so it doubles as a great power plant when it is not fighting. Because it is a Dragon, Ice and Ground attacks hurt it, so keep it behind your tank. If you want an easier Electric option early on, one guide suggests Grizzbolt, the ridable bear with the machine gun. It is a fun first Electric fighter, and it carries you until you can reach a stronger Dragon Pal.

sections.heading: Ice: Frostallion
sections.script: Frostallion is the clear Ice pick, and all the guides I read agree. It is a legendary flying mount, and when you ride it, your attacks become Ice and your Ice damage is boosted. That is wonderful against Dragon bosses, because Ice is the answer to Dragon. Several guides place it in the top tier overall. Remember that it is not a freebie. In the endgame guide on this channel, we noted that Frostallion waits at a frozen lake in the Astral Mountains at level sixty, so bring Fire Pals and warm gear. If you only get one legendary fighter, this is a very safe choice, and you can fly with it too. Frostallion is also a good way to deal with the many Dragon enemies you meet near the end of the game, which is why so many players treat it as a must have.

sections.heading: Ground: Anubis
sections.script: For Ground, the guides point to Anubis. One calls it an elite melee fighter that dodges well, and the other highlights its wide spinning kick and shockwave attacks that hit groups of enemies, including Electric Pals. Its partner skill grants a sidestep and a powerful Ground Smash. Anubis is also a famous base worker with top level Handiwork, which is why so many players already have one. That makes it a bargain, because the same Pal can build your base and protect it. One breeding recipe on this channel uses Astegon and Blazamut to make Anubis, so check our breeding guides if you do not have one yet. A single Anubis with a strong passive skill can serve as your front line fighter and your builder at the same time, which is hard to beat for value.

sections.heading: Dark: Necromus and Shadowbeak
sections.script: Dark has two great answers. Necromus is the pick of two guides, with elite Dark damage, twin spear charges and the title of fastest ground mount. Shadowbeak is the other star, and one guide ranks it in the top tier because of its high Dark damage and powerful skills. Another guide says Shadowbeak has a Dark Laser beam. The raid Pal Bellanoir Libero is also mentioned, and one guide says it has the strongest raw stats of all, but you must earn it from a raid egg, so it is not a standard catch. For most players, Necromus and Shadowbeak are the realistic choices.

sections.heading: Dragon: Jetragon
sections.script: Dragon belongs to Jetragon, and the guides do not argue about this one. It has the highest attack, and the fastest flight, and it fires a homing missile from the air. One guide calls it the undisputed number one. There is one catch. Guides note that its missile cannot stun bosses, so it works best with a partner that can break the boss's guard. Jetragon is also a Dragon, so it is weak to Ice, which is worth remembering in a team fight. Our endgame guide notes that Jetragon is a level seventy Alpha at Dragonmark Peak in Sunreach, so you need to prepare well before you try to catch it.

sections.heading: Neutral: Paladius
sections.script: Neutral is the last element, and the guides agree on Paladius. It hits hard and has strong area pressure, and its partner skill gives you a fast dash. It is among the fastest land mounts, just behind Necromus. Paladius is a ground bruiser, and Necromus is its twin from the desert, which is why they share an arena. One thing to remember from our endgame guide is that Paladius and Necromus are both level sixty, and you can only summon one at a time, so plan two trips. Neutral Pals have no offensive strengths, so Paladius works best as a reliable all round damage dealer instead of a counter.

sections.heading: Build your team
sections.script: Here is the full list of the best picks. Fire has Jormuntide Ignis. Water has Jormuntide or Neptilius. Grass has Lyleen or Verdash. Electric has Orserk. Ice has Frostallion. Ground has Anubis. Dark has Necromus or Shadowbeak. Dragon has Jetragon. Neutral has Paladius. Choose a mix instead of stacking one element, because bosses come with different weaknesses. Rankings can shift between patches, so treat this as a strong baseline. Now it is your turn. Which Pal is the star of your team, and which element would you like a full guide for next? Tell me in the comments. If this guide helped, like the video and subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Palworld guides.
